name: Yogurt Pepper Bowl
ingredients: Oregano, garlic powder, black pepper, lemon juice
instructions: Season the yogurt with oregano, garlic, pepper, and lemon.
Top with pepper, cucumber, and the oil.
doneWhen: Vegetables are raw and the bowl is savory.
tips: A no-cook dinner. Add leftover plain chicken if you are still hungry.

name: Raspberry Yogurt
instructions: Add the raspberries and cinnamon to the yogurt.
Stir once so it stays tart.
doneWhen: Cold, tart, and not sweetened.
tips: Raspberries are the lower-carb berry if you want fruit at dinner.

name: Cottage Cheese and Berries
instructions: Check the tub says no salt added. Regular cottage cheese is too salty for this plan.
Add the berries and cinnamon.
doneWhen: The label says no salt added, and the fruit is on top.
tips: If you can only find regular cottage cheese, skip it. The sodium is several times higher.

name: Cottage Cheese and Apple
instructions: Dice half an apple. Leave the rest for later.
Stir it into the cottage cheese with cinnamon.
doneWhen: Only half an apple is on the plate.
tips: A whole apple pushes the carbs up. Half is the portion.

name: Cottage Cheese, Cucumber, and Dill
instructions: Stir dill, pepper, and lemon into the cottage cheese.
Add the cucumber.
doneWhen: Savory, cold, and made with no-salt-added cottage cheese.
tips: Same rule as breakfast: skip the regular tub.

name: Cottage Cheese and Tomato
instructions: Spoon the cottage cheese into a bowl.
Add tomatoes, herbs, oil, and pepper.
doneWhen: Tomatoes are raw. No mozzarella and no salt.
tips: This is the no-cook stand-in for a caprese.

name: Cottage Cheese and Peppers
ingredients: Black pepper and a squeeze of lemon
instructions: Stir paprika, pepper, and lemon into the cottage cheese.
Eat it with the sliced peppers.
doneWhen: Peppers are raw and the cottage cheese is the no-salt kind.
tips: A light dinner. Pair it with a batch meal earlier in the day if you trained.

name: Cottage Cheese Salsa Bowl
ingredients: Jalapeño or chili flakes, to taste
instructions: Mix tomato, onion, chili, and lime.
Spoon that over the cottage cheese. Do not use jarred salsa.
doneWhen: The salsa is fresh. Jarred salsa is usually salty.
tips: If you need it hotter, add chili flakes, not hot sauce.

name: Boiled Eggs, Yogurt, and Berries
time: About 5 minutes if the eggs are already cooked.
instructions: Use eggs you already cooked, or a carton of pre-cooked eggs.
Peel, pepper them, and eat with the yogurt and berries.
doneWhen: Three eggs and the yogurt are both on the plate.
tips: Boil a few eggs on prep day so breakfast is only peeling.

name: Eggs and Cottage Cheese
time: About 5 minutes if the eggs are already cooked.
instructions: Halve the eggs and pepper them.
Eat them with the cottage cheese and tomatoes.
doneWhen: Eggs are already cooked. Cottage cheese is no-salt-added.
tips: No bread. Tomato is the side.

name: Egg Salad on Cucumber
time: About 5 minutes if the eggs are already cooked.
instructions: Stir the chopped eggs with yogurt, lemon, dill, pepper, and garlic.
Eat it with cucumber slices. No bread.
doneWhen: The salad is bound with yogurt, not mayo.
tips: Make it the same day. Egg salad does not love day three.

name: Eggs on Greens
time: About 5 minutes if the eggs are already cooked.
instructions: Dress the greens with lemon, oil, pepper, and oregano.
Add the eggs. Use the yogurt as the side, or spoon it over the greens.
doneWhen: The greens are raw and the eggs are already cooked.
tips: The yogurt is there for protein. Do not leave it out.

name: Eggs, Yogurt, and Spinach
time: About 5 minutes if the eggs are already cooked.
instructions: Toss the spinach with oil, lemon, and pepper.
Add the eggs and eat the yogurt with them.
doneWhen: Four eggs are on the plate. The spinach is raw.
tips: This is a full dinner. Four eggs is the portion, not two.

name: Eggs and Tomatoes
time: About 5 minutes if the eggs are already cooked.
ingredients: 1 tsp olive oil and black pepper
instructions: Slice the eggs and tomatoes.
Add herbs, oil, and pepper. Eat with the yogurt.
doneWhen: No bread, no cheese, eggs already cooked.
tips: Yogurt makes up the protein the third egg would have missed if you only ate two.

name: Tuna Yogurt Cup
ingredients: 1 can (5 oz) no-salt-added tuna in water, drained
instructions: Drain the tuna. The can must say no salt added.
Stir in yogurt, lemon, dill, and pepper. Eat with cucumber.
doneWhen: Tuna is the no-salt can, mixed and cold.
tips: A savory breakfast. Skip it if that sounds wrong today, and use the berry yogurt instead.

name: Tuna and Cottage Cheese
ingredients: 1 can (5 oz) no-salt-added tuna in water, drained
instructions: Drain the tuna and break it up.
Fold in the cottage cheese, lemon, and pepper. Eat with celery.
doneWhen: Both the tuna and the cottage cheese are no-salt-added.
tips: Regular tuna or regular cottage cheese will blow the sodium.

name: Tuna Celery Salad
ingredients: 1 can (5 oz) no-salt-added tuna in water, drained
instructions: Mix tuna, yogurt, lemon, pepper, and dill.
Eat it over the greens with the celery.
doneWhen: No mayo and no salted tuna.
tips: One can is one meal. Do not split it and call the rest a salad.

name: Tuna and Tomato
ingredients: 1 can (5 oz) no-salt-added tuna in water, drained
instructions: Put the tuna on the greens.
Add tomato, oil, oregano, lemon, and pepper.
doneWhen: Oil is measured. Tuna is no-salt-added.
tips: A spoon of oil is plenty. The tuna is the meal.

name: Tuna, Cucumber, and Avocado
ingredients: 1 can (5 oz) no-salt-added tuna in water, drained
instructions: Plate the greens, cucumber, and tuna.
Add a quarter of an avocado, lime, and pepper.
doneWhen: Avocado is a quarter, not the whole fruit.
tips: The rest of the avocado keeps until tomorrow if you leave the pit in and cover it.

name: Tuna Cabbage Slaw
ingredients: 1 can (5 oz) no-salt-added tuna in water, drained
Lemon, pepper, and a pinch of chili flakes
instructions: Toss cabbage with yogurt, oil, lemon, pepper, and chili.
Fold in the tuna.
doneWhen: The slaw is creamy from yogurt, not mayo.
tips: Cabbage holds up in the fridge if you want to mix it in the morning.

name: Chicken Yogurt Bowl
time: About 5 minutes. Uses chicken you already cooked.
ingredients: 4 oz plain cooked chicken breast, sliced
Dill, lemon, garlic powder, black pepper
instructions: Use leftover plain chicken, or no-salt-added canned chicken, drained.
Season the yogurt and eat it with the chicken and cucumber.
doneWhen: The chicken has no sauce and no brine.
tips: Rotisserie chicken from the store is usually brined. Use the batch you cooked.

name: Chicken and Boiled Eggs
time: About 5 minutes. Nothing new to cook.
instructions: Slice the chicken and eggs.
Pepper them, add lemon, and eat with the vegetables.
doneWhen: Both the chicken and the eggs were cooked on another day.
tips: This is how a prep day pays off. No pot in the morning.

name: Chicken on Greens
time: About 5 minutes. Uses chicken you already cooked.
instructions: Slice the chicken.
Dress the greens with oil, lemon, pepper, and oregano. Add the chicken.
doneWhen: Chicken is plain. Dressing is oil and lemon, not a bottle.
tips: Bottled dressing is where the salt hides.

name: Chicken Cucumber Plate
time: About 5 minutes. Uses chicken you already cooked.
instructions: Stir dill, lemon, and pepper into the yogurt.
Eat it with the chicken and cucumber.
doneWhen: Yogurt is a spoon of sauce, and the chicken is the serving.
tips: Same chicken as the batch pot. Cold is fine.

name: Chicken and Tomatoes
time: About 5 minutes. Uses chicken you already cooked.
instructions: Slice the chicken and tomatoes.
Add oil, herbs, and pepper.
doneWhen: No cheese and no bottled glaze.
tips: Five ounces is a dinner. Four is a lunch.

name: Chicken Pepper Plate
time: About 5 minutes. Uses chicken you already cooked.
ingredients: Paprika, garlic powder, lemon, black pepper
instructions: Slice the chicken and peppers.
Dress with oil, paprika, garlic, lemon, and pepper.
doneWhen: Peppers are raw. Chicken is already cooked.
tips: If the chicken is dry, the lemon and oil fix it. Salt does not need to.

name: Salmon Yogurt Bowl
instructions: Drain the salmon. Use the no-salt can, not smoked salmon.
Mix with yogurt, dill, lemon, and pepper. Eat with cucumber.
doneWhen: Salmon is canned with no salt, or leftover plain salmon.
tips: Smoked salmon looks convenient and is usually cured in salt. Leave it.

name: Salmon and Eggs
time: About 5 minutes. Nothing new to cook.
ingredients: 3 oz plain cooked or no-salt canned salmon
instructions: Plate the salmon and eggs.
Add lemon, dill, and the vegetables.
doneWhen: Eggs are already cooked. Salmon is plain.
tips: Leftover sous vide salmon is ideal here, cold.

name: Salmon Cucumber Bowl
instructions: Flake the salmon.
Add cucumber, yogurt, dill, lemon, and pepper.
doneWhen: No crackers. Cucumber is the crunch.
tips: Bones in canned salmon are soft and add calcium. Mash them in if you don't mind.

name: Salmon on Greens (No cook, greens)
instructions: Dress the greens with oil, lemon, pepper, and dill.
Add the salmon.
doneWhen: Dressing is oil and lemon only.
tips: Cold salmon, hot day. That is the point.

name: Salmon and Tomato
ingredients: Basil or dill, lemon, black pepper
instructions: Plate the salmon and tomatoes.
Add oil, herbs, lemon, and pepper.
doneWhen: No bread and no salted salmon.
tips: Leftover plain salmon works the same as the can.

name: Salmon and Avocado
instructions: Put the salmon on the spinach.
Add a quarter avocado, lime, and pepper.
doneWhen: Avocado is a quarter. Salmon is no-salt-added.
tips: A full dinner without turning the stove on.

name: Oregano Chicken Egg Bake
instructions: Oil the pot. Stir chicken, eggs, whites, zucchini, and spices.
Cook on LOW. Check at 2.5 hours. Chicken should be 165°F.
Rest 10 minutes. Cut into 4 boxes.
doneWhen: The protein is cooked through and boxed in even portions.
tips: Mediterranean herbs, no bread. A batch breakfast. Fridge 3 days.

name: Lemon Chicken and Eggs
instructions: Bag the chicken with zest, oregano, pepper, and oil. Cook at 150°F.
Add the eggs for the last 13 minutes at 167°F, or boil them ahead.
Each box is 4 oz chicken and 1 egg, finished with lemon.
doneWhen: The protein is cooked through and boxed in even portions.
tips: Protein first. Lemon stands in for salt.

name: Tomato Oregano Chicken
instructions: Put chicken, tomatoes, garlic, oregano, pepper, and oil in the pot.
LOW 4 hours. Shred and divide into 4.
Eat the chicken before the tomatoes.
doneWhen: The protein is cooked through and boxed in even portions.
tips: Mediterranean plate: chicken, tomato, olive oil, oregano. No pasta.

name: Chicken on Lemon Greens
instructions: Bag chicken with pepper and oregano. 150°F for 1.5–2 hours.
Dress greens with oil and lemon.
4 oz chicken on a large plate of greens.
doneWhen: The protein is cooked through and boxed in even portions.
tips: Eat the chicken first, then the greens.

name: Lemon Fennel Chicken
instructions: Put chicken and fennel in the pot with garlic, lemon, oil, and pepper.
LOW 4 hours. Fennel should be soft.
4 portions. Chicken first.
doneWhen: The protein is cooked through and boxed in even portions.
tips: Fennel and lemon are the Mediterranean side. Fridge 4 days.

name: Garlic Oregano Chicken
instructions: Bag chicken with garlic, oregano, oil, and pepper.
150°F for 1.5–2 hours. Sear 30 seconds if you want.
Serve with raw or warmed zucchini and lemon. 5 oz chicken.
doneWhen: The protein is cooked through and boxed in even portions.
tips: A small dinner plate. No rice.

name: Turkey Pepper Egg Bake
instructions: Brown nothing. Stir turkey, eggs, whites, pepper, and spices.
LOW only, 2.5–3.5 hours, until 165°F.
4 portions.
doneWhen: The protein is cooked through and boxed in even portions.
tips: Use breast meat, not a salty sausage blend.

name: Turkey and Eggs
instructions: Bag the turkey with paprika and pepper. 150°F.
Cook eggs to jammy, 167°F for 13 minutes.
4 oz turkey and 1 egg, with lemon.
doneWhen: The protein is cooked through and boxed in even portions.
tips: Soft enough if you slice the turkey thin.
